sections.title: Anchor state — the on-chain footprint
sections.key_moment: Picking `bytes32` for the blob ID. Walrus blob IDs are exactly 32 bytes (a BLAKE2b-256 hash of the content), so they slot into a single storage word — one SSTORE per anchor regardless of underlying blob size. Using `string` or `bytes` would double the cost and break the constant-gas property.

sections.title: The write path — `anchor(bytes32 blobId)`
sections.key_moment: Using `msg.sender` as the mapping key (rather than taking an `address owner` parameter). This makes the on-chain authentication implicit — the EVM has already proven who the caller is by the time we reach this line, so we don't need any explicit `require(msg.sender == owner)` check.

sections.title: The read path — `blobOf(address)` and the equivalence gate
sections.key_moment: The read path is a plain mapping lookup with no decoding, no aggregation, and no events — the off-chain client uses the returned `bytes32` to build a URL like `https://aggregator.walrus-testnet.walrus.space/v1/blobs/<blobId-as-base64url>` and fetches the actual content from there. The contract's job ends at returning the pointer.
